messages.subject: Legend manipulation
parts:
for(i in unique(df$temp)) {
  
    df_i <- df[df$temp == i, ]
    
      my.plot <- ggplot(df_i, aes(x = Year, y = Average_Total_Animal_Consumption), color) +

      geom_point(aes(colour = factor(paste0(Class, " ", Model)), size = 7, shape= Model)) +
        
      geom_point(colour="grey90", size = 1.5)+
       
      labs(x = "Year",    y = "Value", title = paste("Lab Run ", prettyNum(i, ","))) +

       scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2100, by = 10))+

    print(my.plot)
}

I spent a lot of time learning how to do what I have already (never used ggplot2 before)...

I am satisfied with everything except the legend.

The left corner has 
-Size legend as a dot 7 (I do not want this)
-Title of colour in the legend shows: factor(paste0(Class, " ", Model)) I need that to be anything else like "Scenario"
-Shape is model, but I want that to be Source.

I tried guides and labs, and that is not solving my issue. I haven't found the solution, and help is greatly appreciated!

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Legend manipulation
parts:
Hi:

Your example is not reproducible, and you have a number of programming
infelicities.

1. You should not define a factor inside a ggplot() call - create it
in the data before you call ggplot().
2. The loop is unnecessary. This would be easier to do if you split
the data into a list by unique levels of df$temp first; then, you
could write a simple function to produce a single ggplot and map it
across the components of the list.
3. Your first legend issue pertains to a misunderstanding between plot
aesthetics that are set to constant values and those that are mapped
to variables. Only aesthetic _mappings_ should be defined in aes();
all set aesthetic (e.g., size = 7) should be defined outside the aes()
call.
4. There is no reason to call the same geom twice on the same data set.
5. You said that "Shape is model, but I want that to be Source" -
unfortunately, you mapped shape to the Model variable in your first
geom_point() call.
6. The labs() function can be used to define titles for legends
according to the name of the aesthetic; e.g.,
labs(x = "my x label", y = "my y label", colour = "my legend")

Without having a real clue about what you're doing, here's a skeleton
of how you might improve your code. This is not at all tested, so
caveat emptor!

df$Class_Model <- <define>
my_list <- split(df, df$temp) # creates a list
my_labs <- paste(:"Lab Run", seq(length(my_list)))

gplot <- function(x, idx)
{
ggplot(x, aes(x = Year, y = Average_Total_Animal_Consumption)) +
geom_point(aes(colour = Class_Model, shape = Source), size = 7) +
labs(y = "Value", color = idx) +

It's not clear what you want to do with the plots (save them to
objects, print them, send them to a document file, ???), but perhaps
the simplest way to accommodate the widest range of possibilities is
to save the plot objects in a list - then you can decide what to do
with them. Since you have two inputs to the function, we can run a
loop:

plot_list <- vector("list", length(my_list))
for(i in seq_along(plot_list)) plot_list[[i]] <- gplot(my_list[[i]],
my_labs[i])


If you need more specific help, please provide a reproducible example,
(Google 'R reproducible example' - there should be at least half a
dozen excellent guides at the top of the results list.)

Dennis
